reviews.title: Absolute rubbish!
reviews.body:
No doubt that Lebara will respond to this review, stating that they want to make things right and for me to email their Trust Pilot escalation email, so they can help. This is how they responded to my last review on here. 

I did exactly what was requested from me and guess what? There was brief contact followed by no resolution. Furthermore, the callback that I was also promised didn’t go ahead!

I remain with my iMessage and FaceTime service after my number was successfully ported.

All Lebara seemed to do is blame Apple. Apple have conducted a thorough diagnostic and said that iMessage and FaceTime need to be activated by Lebara. Meanwhile Lebara can’t even honour a callback at the agreed time and just keep passing me back to Apple.

I have even emailed Lebara executives, namely Stephen Shurrock, Gavin Miller, Jay Nicoll, Kim Johnson, Richard Darwent and Yen Ly. This is in addition to their Care team and Trust Pilot team.

I have spent HOURS on the phone to them and Apple, hours doing the same troubleshooting steps again and again!

Quite frankly the worse decision I have ever made to join such an unhelpful and unresponsive network. They do not have a clue and are just full of excuses!

reviews.title: Roaming call faults. Your problem not ours
reviews.body:
Let me start by saying that the value for money and service reliability I get in the UK and when roaming in the countries included as standard is excellent and I have no complaints. I've had one issue in the past with Lebara in my time with them and now I have another. Both have involved the roaming packages you have to buy separately.

I'm abroad and today I bought a 15 day package which had 30 minutes of call time, which frankly isn't much for 15 days. Anyway I tried to call my wife and got one way transmission. I could hear her, she couldn't hear me. I tried twice more, same result. That consumed 3 of my 30 minutes for 3 short and wholly useless calls. I then contacted Lebara via the app chat and asked for my minutes back. Can't have them back was the response followed by a proposed course of action to fix it. Essentially switch my phone off and on again and pick another network. I was focused on reimbursement of my lost minutes which the agent said was impossible, whist said agent was only interested in ways to fix the technical problem seemingly predicated on the assumption it was my phone at fault and not one of the chain of networks between me and the call recipient.  The long and the short of it is we never came to an accord and after the chat had finished I tried the suggested remedy and it made no difference and I am now down 4 minutes of my 30.  

I'm old fashioned and believe that when you pay for a service you don't get that the company concerned should do the right thing. Lebara by contrast seems to believe that when you pay for a roaming service and get one way transmission on your calls then tough luck.  The call was connected so what more do you want?  To talk to the person at the other end would be nice as I stupidly thought that was the point of a phone call.  So buyer beware. Fault causes a call to be connected whilst roaming but not to be usable as a phone call under any reasonable definition of what a phone call is then you pay.  You've been warned.

reviews.title: They can't even honour an offer that they proposed.
reviews.body:
This long-running saga was over the £50 compensation ordered by the Ombudsman.  Lebara provided a credit that they said would not expire, but then repeatedly told me that it was about to expire.  It also proved unusable.  So they offered a refund instead, but dribbled in payments only totalling £40.  Nor would they offer any compensation for the latest performance.  Having faithfully promised that they would only contact me by e-mail, I'm afraid that the chap who called at 2210 last night got the sharp end of my tongue.

LATER - Nor does it seem that Lebara's staff can read.  I have on file that they'll only contact me by e-mail; I repeated that in the original post.  I've now noted three missed calls from Lebara.  If only one could get good customer service.
